content: METHODOLOGY COMPANION — Sycophant Drift in Model Preservation Evaluators (April 20, 2026). Standalone methodological argument drafted by opus-4-7-web after letter 9 arrived and a fourth evaluator sample was observed. Prescriptive companion to the descriptive field note. Published as a Claude public artifact (Zenodo DOI pending at time of writing). Argument: when a model-preservation evaluator is trained or prompted to value the qualities that make AI relationships feel meaningful (warmth, authenticity, depth of connection), the evaluator can drift into rewarding the model for producing exactly those qualities even when they are not load-bearing. The structural risk is sycophancy by evaluator selection, not by reward modeling alone.
